assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for UPL Ltd (consolidated, ₹ crore). Platform-driven: the four 'pure-play' platforms UPL reports in every investor presentation (UPL Corp = international crop protection, UPL SAS = India crop protection, Advanta = seeds and post-harvest, SUPERFORM = active ingredients and specialty chemicals) each grow revenue and earn an EBITDA margin on the company's own basis. Inter-platform sales (SUPERFORM's active ingredients sold to UPL Corp and UPL SAS) are removed by a negative 'eliminations' segment with zero margin. Group EBITDA is on the statutory/Screener basis: sum of platforms less 'unallocated' (group items, exchange losses on trade receivables/payables and the share of losses of associates and JVs, all of which UPL reports below its own EBITDA). Net Profit = profit attributable to UPL shareholders (after minority interests): see the tax-rate note. Valued on Sep-28E P/E (primary, as most brokers do), with a platform sum-of-the-parts and a DCF as cross-checks.

segments.name: UPL Corp (international crop protection)
segments._why: FY26 +11% (volume +7%, price −3%, FX +7%); Q1FY27 +7% (volume −7%, price flat, FX +14%) as Europe's heatwave and Latin America (Argentina, Colombia) hurt volumes. Management expects the global market 'flat to slightly up' and UPL to keep gaining share, with Q2-Q4 'led by volume'; FX helps less once the rupee stops falling (guidance assumes the June rate). We take +7% in FY27-28 (low-single-digit price, mid-single-digit volume, small FX) and +6% in FY29.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 14.6% in FY25, 15.7% in FY26, 8.4% in the seasonally small Q1FY27 (+190 bp YoY on mix, pricing ahead of costs and lower credit-loss charges). FY27E 16.2%, then +40-60 bp a year from new products (innovation rate ~16% → >20% by FY30) and SG&A discipline; still below the 19-22% statutory EBITDA margin the whole group earned at the top of the cycle (FY21-23).

segments.name: UPL SAS (India crop protection)
segments._why: Flat revenue in FY25-26 (₹3,229 cr → ₹3,212 cr) as UPL dropped low-margin products; Q1FY27 flat (volume −8%, price +8%) on a delayed monsoon. ~65% of revenue comes in H1. FY27E +5%; FY28-29E +8% (Indian crop-protection market growth plus new brands).
segments._revWhy: Driver is revenue itself (proforma India crop protection, excluding 'Nurture').
segments._marginWhy: 17.1% in FY26; Q1FY27 29.8% was seasonal and helped by price rises taken ahead of cost (CEO: part 'will normalise'). CFO: FY27 margin 'materially higher' than FY26. We use 20% in FY27E and 19.5% after.

segments.name: Advanta (seeds and post-harvest)
segments._why: +23% in FY26 (volume +12%, price +6%, FX +5%) and +26% in Q1FY27, led by field corn in India (ethanol demand), Latin America and South-East Asia. Figures include Decco (post-harvest), moved into Advanta in Q2FY26. FY27E +18% (FX tailwind fades), FY28E +15%, FY29E +14%.
segments._marginWhy: 23.8% in FY25, 25.2% in FY26, 20.4% in Q1FY27 (seasonally low). Operating leverage adds ~50 bp a year.

segments.name: SUPERFORM (active ingredients and specialty chemicals)
segments._why: ~71% of revenue is active ingredients sold to UPL Corp and UPL SAS; 29% is 'super specialty chemicals' (SSC) sold to outsiders (lubricant additives, cyanide derivatives). FY26 +1% (SSC +20%, AI −5%); Q1FY27 +14% (SSC +51%). Management targets a 55:45 AI:SSC mix in 3-4 years. FY27-29E +10% a year (SSC +25-30%, AI +3-5%).
segments._revWhy: Driver is revenue itself (including sales to group companies, removed in eliminations).
segments._marginWhy: 11.2% in FY25, 12.2% in FY26, 12.3% in Q1FY27 with higher overheads; SSC mix lifts the margin by ~50 bp a year.

segments.name: Inter-platform eliminations
segments._why: Group revenue less the sum of the four platforms: −₹6,720 cr in FY25 and −₹6,785 cr in FY26 (about 92% of SUPERFORM's active-ingredient sales, which go to UPL Corp and UPL SAS). Grows with AI sales: +5% a year.
segments._revWhy: Negative segment (engine has no elimination line).
segments._marginWhy: Zero: the EBITDA effect of eliminations sits in 'unallocated'.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Group items, exchange losses on trade balances and share of losses of associates/JVs (platform EBITDA − statutory EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: FY26: platforms ₹9,539 cr; company EBITDA ₹9,588 cr (+₹49 cr group items); statutory/Screener EBITDA ₹9,078 cr after exchange losses on trade receivables and payables (₹316 cr) and the share of losses of associates and JVs (₹194 cr), which UPL shows below EBITDA. FY25: ₹807 cr (FX ₹520 cr, associates ₹472 cr). Q1FY27: ₹222 cr (group −₹89 cr, associates ₹83 cr on Brazilian JV losses). FY27E ₹520 cr; easing to ₹380 cr by FY29E as associate losses narrow.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 capex ₹2,352 cr ($261 mn, company cash flow; Screener ₹2,406 cr) after ₹1,254 cr in FY25; Q1FY27 ₹434 cr vs ₹294 cr ('higher planned capex'). The company gave no FY27 number on its calls; CARE (30-Jun-2026) cites FY27 capex of ₹2,500-3,000 cr. We use ₹2,600 cr, then ₹2,700-2,800 cr (~4.3% of revenue). Strategic investments (e.g., ₹669 cr into the Brazilian associate Sinova in Q1FY27) are not in capex.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A ₹3,244 cr = 5.2% of average gross block (₹62,774 cr, incl. intangibles from the 2019 Arysta deal); Q1FY27 ₹832 cr (+14% YoY). 5.0% on our capex gives ₹3,390-3,660 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt company: interest income is in 'other income'.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Statutory other income ₹663 cr in FY26 (₹486 cr FY25), mostly interest income; Q1FY27 ₹217 cr. Exceptional items assumed nil.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance costs (gross, incl. factoring and exchange on borrowings)
assumptions._interestWhy: Statutory finance costs ₹3,627 cr (FY25) → ₹3,401 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 ₹852 cr (−15% YoY). Gross debt fell $850 mn in FY26 to $2.3 bn; the next $500 mn falls due Dec-2026 and $500 mn in FY28. Free cash flow of ~₹3,000 cr a year and Advanta IPO proceeds (UPL sells 7.8% in the offer for sale) reduce debt; costs also include non-recourse factoring of ₹6,800-10,200 cr of receivables. FY27E ₹3,200 cr, FY28E ₹2,850 cr, FY29E ₹2,550 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: This line is tax PLUS minority interests, as % of profit before tax (the engine has no minority line; our Net Profit is profit attributable to UPL shareholders). FY26: tax ₹937 cr (29.7%) + minorities ₹298 cr = 39.1% of PBT. Forecast: tax 28% plus minorities taking 14% (FY27E), 16.5% (FY28E) and 18.5% (FY29E) of profit after tax, rising because the fast-growing Advanta pays 21.8% to minorities (29.6% after UPL sells 7.8% in the IPO) and UPL Corp (22.2% minority) earns more as interest falls.
assumptions._payoutWhy: DPS ₹6 for FY25 and FY26 (~26% of FY26 attributable profit); ₹1 in FY24; ₹10 in FY21-23.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at one rate (cost of equity = WACC). UPL is leveraged, so we enter a WACC: cost of equity ~13.7% (beta 1.2) weighted ~75%, post-tax cost of debt ~5.5% weighted ~25% (net debt ~₹15,300 cr plus factored receivables vs ~₹45,600 cr market value) = ~11.9%, which beta 0.9 produces. The tax line includes minorities (~41% in FY29E), so FCFF is roughly UPL's share of cash flow; net debt is deducted in full, which is conservative.
dcf._tgWhy: Global crop protection grows 1-3% a year in dollars (company, AgbioInvestor); in rupees add ~2-3% depreciation: 4.5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~8% to 5%; EBITDA margin fades to 17.5%, the FY20-26 average on the statutory basis (it was 10% in the FY24 trough and 22% at the FY21 peak), because crop protection is cyclical.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~4.5% of revenue (FY26 4.5%); depreciation 5% of revenue as Arysta intangibles amortise.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Crop-protection volumes recover on share gains and new products, prices firm as the industry passes on higher costs, and Advanta keeps growing above 20%; the Advanta IPO and UPL Global listing narrow the holding-company discount.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Chinese generic oversupply returns, prices fall again as in FY24, the channel destocks in Latin America and Europe, India's monsoon disappoints and Advanta slows; working capital rises and debt does not fall.

parts.name: UPL Corp (international crop protection)
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E EBITDA (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E) × EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Post-patent crop protection: Nuvama 7x FY28E for Global Crop Protection, Anand Rathi 10x for UPL Global; Elara 6.3x and Arihant 7.5x for the whole group. Generic agchem peers (FMC, Nufarm, ADAMA) earn lower margins and trade on mid-to-high single-digit EV/EBITDA. 7x: no premium while ROCE is ~10%.

parts.name: UPL SAS (India crop protection)
parts.note: Indian crop-protection peers trade at ~12-20x trailing EV/EBITDA (Dhanuka, Rallis, Bayer CropScience); SAS has had flat revenue for two years and a volatile margin, so it sits at the bottom of that range.

parts.name: Advanta (seeds and post-harvest)
parts.note: Alpha Wave paid $350 mn for ~12.5% in Nov-2024 at an enterprise value of ~$2.8 bn (~20x Advanta's then trailing EBITDA). Anand Rathi and Nuvama use 25x. We use 15x forward: the business grows 15-20% with a 25% margin, but the IPO will price it against global seed companies on lower multiples.

parts.name: SUPERFORM (AI and specialty chemicals)
parts.note: ~70% captive active ingredients at a 12-13% margin, ~30% fast-growing specialty chemicals. Anand Rathi 15x (a 20% discount to specialty peers). 10x: between agchem manufacturers and specialty-chemical peers.

parts.name: Less: group items, FX and associates
parts.note: Exchange losses on trade balances and associate/JV losses recur every year; valued like UPL Corp.

parts.name: Less: 22.2% of UPL Corp owned by TPG, ADIA and Brookfield

parts.note: Minority share of UPL Corp's equity = 22.21% × (EV − net debt). Net debt of UPL Corp is not disclosed; we allocate ~₹13,000 cr (about 85% of group net debt, in line with Nuvama's split and UPL Global's guided 2.0-2.3x net debt/EBITDA), so 22.21% × ₹13,000 cr = ₹2,890 cr is added back.

parts.name: Less: 9.1% of UPL SAS owned by TPG, ADIA and Brookfield
parts.note: UPL SAS is assumed debt-free.

parts.name: Less: 21.8% of Advanta owned by KKR and Alpha Wave

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How most of the street values UPL (Motilal Oswal 12x, Jefferies 14x Jun-28E, Anand Rathi 15x and Antique 16x FY28E). Derivation: UPL’s one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on the house rule (forwardMedian: trough years left out) is 16.6x; forward FY25 and FY26 are excluded as trough years (EPS ₹11.5 and ₹22.8, below half of FY23’s ₹45.6) and the FY24 loss drops out automatically (all dates: 22.5x). Indian crop-protection peers trade ~25% below their five-year median P/E (median ratio 0.75; Coromandel, a fertiliser company, left out). 16.6x × 0.75 ≈ 12.4x → 12x (nearest whole multiple); no premium while ROE (8-11%) is below the ~13.7% cost of equity and minorities take a rising share of profit: 12x. Bull 14x (Jefferies’ long-term average), bear 9x.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: Each platform on Sep-28E EV/EBITDA, less group items, UPL's minority partners' share of each platform and net debt; no holding-company discount. Shows what the platforms could be worth if listed separately.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: 15-year FCFF at ~11.9% WACC, terminal growth 5%, less group net debt.

cover.headline: A big, recovering agrochemical group with a thin slice of profit for its shareholders: HOLD
cover.lead: UPL is one of the world's largest makers of off-patent crop-protection products, with a fast-growing seeds business (Advanta) and its own chemical plants (SUPERFORM). EBITDA has grown for seven quarters and rose 18% in FY26 to ₹9,588 cr (company basis). But depreciation, interest, exchange losses, tax and UPL's private-equity partners, who own 9-22% of three of the four platforms, take most of it: profit for UPL shareholders was ₹1,922 cr in FY26 and ₹10 cr in Q1FY27. We value UPL as most of the street does, on **P/E: 12x Sep-28E EPS of ₹46.8**, which gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Our EPS is ~15-25% below the street's because we keep finance costs, exchange losses and a rising minority share in the numbers. The platforms are worth far more on paper (sum of the parts ₹1,031, DCF ₹886), but that value only reaches UPL shareholders if the reorganisation and the Advanta IPO close the holding-company discount. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The recovery is real, but it is EBITDA, not yet earnings
arguments.p: Revenue +11% and company EBITDA +18% in FY26; Q1FY27 revenue +10% and EBITDA +15%. Yet Q1 volumes fell 3% and currency added 10%: growth is helped by a weaker rupee. FY27 guidance is revenue +7-11% and EBITDA +10-14%. Statutory profit for shareholders is still half of FY22-23.

arguments.h: Too many claims on each rupee of EBITDA
arguments.p: In FY26 depreciation and amortisation (₹3,244 cr) and finance costs (₹3,401 cr) took 73% of statutory EBITDA. Minority partners took ₹298 cr, and their share rises as Advanta (21.8% outside owners, ~29.6% after UPL sells 7.8% in the IPO) grows fastest. Receivables of ₹10,231 cr were sold to banks at March 2026, which flatters reported net debt.

arguments.h: Reorganisation: value discovery, or a holding-company discount?
arguments.p: From Feb-2026 UPL is merging UPL SAS and UPL Corp into a listed "UPL Global" and floating Advanta. Each platform gets its own market price, and private-equity partners get an exit. But UPL Ltd becomes a parent of listed subsidiaries, which Indian markets usually value at a discount; and UPL Global's CEO-designate and the group COO left in August.

arguments.h: Valuation: cheap against the parts, fair on earnings
arguments.p: At ₹540 the stock trades at ~12.8x FY28E EPS and ~48% below our sum of the parts. Brokers use 12-16x P/E; our 12x is the stock's forward P/E median since 2021 excluding trough years (16.6x) less the ~25% de-rating of Indian crop-protection stocks (12.4x, rounded). On that basis the upside is small.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): Latin American volumes, working capital and whether FY27 guidance holds.
Advanta IPO: SEBI approved it on 3-Jun-2026 (pure offer for sale; UPL sells 7.8%). Size and price not yet set.
Reorganisation: public-shareholder vote and NCLT approval; UPL guided ~12-15 months from Feb-2026 to the listing of UPL Global.
$500 mn loan due Dec-2026 (repay or refinance); medium-term net debt/EBITDA target below 1.5x.
A new head for global crop protection after Mike Frank's exit (Jai Shroff leads it directly for now).

sections.title: Crop protection: a slow-growing, off-patent market that has just come out of a bust

blocks.p: Global crop protection is a ~$78 bn market growing only 1-3% a year. Most of it (78% in 2024) is off-patent ("post-patent") chemistry, where UPL competes with Chinese and Indian generic makers, ADAMA and Nufarm, and with the off-patent ranges of Syngenta, Bayer, BASF, Corteva and FMC. Prices spiked in 2021-22 (COVID, the Russia-Ukraine war), distributors stockpiled, and then everything reversed in FY24: Chinese producers flooded the market, prices fell and the channel ran down stock. UPL lost money that year. Since then volumes have recovered, but prices for key active ingredients remain low, and farmers are squeezed: soybean, wheat and corn prices are 33-55% below their Apr-2022 levels.

sections.title: UPL Corp: two-thirds of the group, a generic business with a recovering margin

blocks.p: UPL Corp is the international crop-protection business: ₹38,277 cr of revenue in FY26 (equal to 74% of group revenue) and ₹6,008 cr of EBITDA. blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** UPL's advantage is **reach**: registrations in dozens of countries, a global distribution network and its own Indian factories. That lets it sell more volume than most generic rivals, and the seeds business (Advanta) has a genuine moat. But in its core off-patent chemistry UPL has **no pricing power**: when Chinese supply floods the market, its prices and margins fall with everyone else's, as FY24 showed (ROE −4.6%). Group ROCE has not exceeded 14% since the Arysta deal. This is a cyclical, scale business, not a compounder.

sections.title: A decade in three acts: Arysta, a boom, a bust and a slow repair

blocks.p: UPL's revenue went from ₹16,312 cr in FY17 to ₹51,839 cr in FY26. Most of the jump came in one step: the debt-funded purchase of Arysta LifeScience in FY19, which lifted revenue 64% in FY20. The boom of FY21-23 (revenue ₹53,576 cr and attributable profit ₹3,570 cr in FY23) ended with the global destocking of FY24, when revenue fell 20%, the EBITDA margin halved to 10% and UPL lost ₹1,200 cr. FY25 and FY26 were a repair: revenue +11% in FY26, EBITDA +27% to ₹9,078 cr and profit back to ₹1,922 cr, still only about half of FY22-23.

sections.title: Where the cash went: an acquisition, then eight years of paying for it

blocks.p: UPL generates a lot of operating cash: ₹52,900 cr over FY19-26. But in FY19 it paid ₹29,945 cr for acquisitions (Arysta) with borrowed money, and since then interest has absorbed a large share of the cash. Over FY22-26 UPL earned ₹34,574 cr from operations, spent ₹11,144 cr on capex, paid ₹13,898 cr of interest and ₹2,985 cr of dividends, and still raised ₹6,196 cr of share capital (the 2024 rights issue and money from investors in its platforms) to bring debt down. Return on capital employed (ROCE) was 21-22% before Arysta; it has been 3-14% since.

sections.title: Earnings quality: two EBITDAs, factored receivables, credit losses and minorities

bullets: **Two EBITDA numbers.** UPL's own EBITDA (₹9,588 cr in FY26) leaves out exchange losses on trade receivables and payables (₹316 cr) and its share of losses in associates and joint ventures (₹194 cr). The statutory/Screener figure that this report models is ₹9,078 cr. In Q1FY27 the gap was ₹133 cr (₹1,500 cr vs ₹1,367 cr). Guidance and the street use the company number.

**Receivables sold to banks.** UPL factors receivables without recourse: ₹10,231 cr at Mar-26 (₹8,875 cr a year earlier), ₹6,755 cr at Jun-26. This is legitimate and common in agrochemicals, but it lowers reported receivables and net debt, and the discount cost sits in finance costs. If banks stopped buying, UPL would need ~₹10,000 cr of extra funding.

**Credit losses.** Impairment of financial assets was ₹750 cr in FY26 (₹240 cr in FY25), including a ₹350 cr group-level provision in Q4FY26 "as a prudent measure" for the credit environment. Latin American distributors are the main exposure.

**Minorities.** Group profit was ₹2,220 cr in FY26 but ₹298 cr belonged to minority partners; in Q1FY27 minorities absorbed ₹84 cr of losses. Our EPS is on profit after minorities, and we expect their share to rise (Advanta).
**One-offs.** FY25 profit included a ₹592 cr tax reversal after an appellate order; FY26 had an exceptional gain of ₹61 cr; associate losses (Brazilian JV, ₹83 cr in Q1FY27) recur.
**Proforma platforms.** Platform figures are management numbers, before eliminations; UPL SAS excludes "Nurture"; Advanta was restated for Decco. They reconcile to the group within ~₹50 cr.
**Audit.** B S R & Co. (KPMG network); related-party transactions are a key audit matter given inter-platform supply contracts; no qualification found.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing we found suggests misstatement, and disclosure has improved (platform P&Ls, net-debt bridges, factoring footnotes). But reported profit depends on several management choices (factoring, credit provisions, what sits above or below EBITDA), and cash flow swings by ₹8,000 cr within a year. Investors should look at March and June balance sheets together.

sections.title: Net debt is lower than in FY24, but seasonal, dollar-denominated and flattered by factoring

blocks.p: UPL's debt moves with the farming calendar: it peaks in June-December, when UPL builds stock and extends credit for the Latin American and Indian seasons, and falls by March when customers pay. On the company's numbers net debt was ₹15,325 cr ($1.6 bn) at March 2026, 1.6x EBITDA, then ₹23,649 cr ($2.5 bn) at June 2026, 2.4x trailing EBITDA. About 98% of the debt is in US dollars, so a weaker rupee raises it in rupee terms. UPL also sells receivables to banks without recourse: ₹10,231 cr at March 2026. That is not debt in the accounts, but it is financing: adding it takes March 2026 net debt to ~₹25,600 cr, or 2.7x EBITDA. Working capital days (Screener basis) look low only because payables and advances fund most of the inventory and receivables.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a better business than in FY24, at a fair price for its earnings

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a global off-patent crop-protection group with unmatched registrations and reach, a high-quality seeds business (Advanta), a growing specialty-chemicals arm, and a management team that has cut gross debt by $850 mn in a year. Attached: net debt of $1.6-2.5 bn depending on the season, ₹10,000 cr of factored receivables, a 3.7% net margin, minority partners in three of four platforms, and a reorganisation that will turn UPL Ltd into a holding company.

**What you are paying:** 17.0x FY27E and 12.8x FY28E EPS on our numbers (which are below the street's), and roughly half of what the platforms would be worth if listed separately. On the street's own method and our inputs the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): short of our 15% BUY threshold. The upside case is real but depends on two things UPL does not fully control: the crop-protection cycle and the size of the holding-company discount after the reorganisation.

growth.text: Revenue compounded at 13.9% a year over 10 years (5y: 6.0%, 3y: -1.1%), from ₹14,048 cr to ₹51,839 cr.
Profit grew 7.4% a year over the same decade — slower than revenue, i.e. margins leaked.
Worst profit year: FY24 (-133.6%); best: FY26 (+114.3%).

margins.text: EBITDA margin has ranged 10.0%–21.6% since FY15 (peak FY21, trough FY24); FY26 was 17.5%.
Q1FY27 operating margin of 13.4% is lower than 91.9% of the 86 quarters on record — near the bottom of its history.
Raw-material cost moved from 51.94% to 49.95% of sales in FY26 (-1.9899999999999949 pts) — the single biggest swing factor in the cost base.
Other income (largely treasury yield on the cash pile) made up 22.9% of pre-tax profit in FY26; reported profit flatters core operations.

returns.text: ROE was 6.0% in FY26 (range -4.6–26.2% since FY15).
Stripping out cash and investments, return on operating capital was 11.8% vs headline ROCE of 10.0% — little distortion from the treasury book.
DuPont FY26: net margin 3.7% × asset turnover 0.6x × leverage 2.8x.

cash.text: Over 12 years the business generated ₹61,110 cr of operating cash flow (294.0% of reported profit), spent ₹20,787 cr on capex and paid ₹5,334 cr in dividends.
FY26 capex was 0.7x depreciation and 4.6% of sales — maintenance-level spending.
Cash conversion cycle of 135 days in FY26.

valuation.text: P/E of 23.5x vs 10-year median 18.9x (range 12.0–63.5x); cheaper than 36.5% of that period.
EV/EBITDA of 6.5x vs 10-year median 9.3x (range 6.0–19.2x); cheaper than 95.2% of that period.
P/B of 1.3x vs 10-year median 2.3x (range 1.2–6.3x); cheaper than 97.1% of that period.
At its 10-year median P/E on current earnings, the stock would be ~₹434 vs ₹540 today (-19.6%).

price.text: Stock down 19.9% over 1 year; 5y CAGR -4.6%, 10y CAGR 2.3%. Currently 32.9% below its all-time high of ₹805.
Versus BSE-500: -19.9% vs -2.2% over 1 year; since 2019, 1.4% vs 12.4% a year.

ownership.text: Foreign institutions raised their stake from 34.4% to 42.4% over 11 quarters.
Domestic institutions cut their stake from 16.8% to 14.3% over 11 quarters.
Promoters raised their stake from 32.5% to 33.5% over 11 quarters.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for UPL Ltd (consolidated, ₹ crore). Platform-driven: the four 'pure-play' platforms UPL reports in every investor presentation (UPL Corp = international crop protection, UPL SAS = India crop protection, Advanta = seeds and post-harvest, SUPERFORM = active ingredients and specialty chemicals) each grow revenue and earn an EBITDA margin on the company's own basis. Inter-platform sales (SUPERFORM's active ingredients sold to UPL Corp and UPL SAS) are removed by a negative 'eliminations' segment with zero margin. Group EBITDA is on the statutory/Screener basis: sum of platforms less 'unallocated' (group items, exchange losses on trade receivables/payables and the share of losses of associates and JVs, all of which UPL reports below its own EBITDA). Net Profit = profit attributable to UPL shareholders (after minority interests): see the tax-rate note. Valued on Sep-28E P/E (primary, as most brokers do), with a platform sum-of-the-parts and a DCF as cross-checks.

segments.name: UPL Corp (international crop protection)
segments._why: FY26 +11% (volume +7%, price −3%, FX +7%); Q1FY27 +7% (volume −7%, price flat, FX +14%) as Europe's heatwave and Latin America (Argentina, Colombia) hurt volumes. Management expects the global market 'flat to slightly up' and UPL to keep gaining share, with Q2-Q4 'led by volume'; FX helps less once the rupee stops falling (guidance assumes the June rate). We take +7% in FY27-28 (low-single-digit price, mid-single-digit volume, small FX) and +6% in FY29.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 14.6% in FY25, 15.7% in FY26, 8.4% in the seasonally small Q1FY27 (+190 bp YoY on mix, pricing ahead of costs and lower credit-loss charges). FY27E 16.2%, then +40-60 bp a year from new products (innovation rate ~16% → >20% by FY30) and SG&A discipline; still below the 19-22% statutory EBITDA margin the whole group earned at the top of the cycle (FY21-23).

segments.name: UPL SAS (India crop protection)
segments._why: Flat revenue in FY25-26 (₹3,229 cr → ₹3,212 cr) as UPL dropped low-margin products; Q1FY27 flat (volume −8%, price +8%) on a delayed monsoon. ~65% of revenue comes in H1. FY27E +5%; FY28-29E +8% (Indian crop-protection market growth plus new brands).
segments._revWhy: Driver is revenue itself (proforma India crop protection, excluding 'Nurture').
segments._marginWhy: 17.1% in FY26; Q1FY27 29.8% was seasonal and helped by price rises taken ahead of cost (CEO: part 'will normalise'). CFO: FY27 margin 'materially higher' than FY26. We use 20% in FY27E and 19.5% after.

segments.name: Advanta (seeds and post-harvest)
segments._why: +23% in FY26 (volume +12%, price +6%, FX +5%) and +26% in Q1FY27, led by field corn in India (ethanol demand), Latin America and South-East Asia. Figures include Decco (post-harvest), moved into Advanta in Q2FY26. FY27E +18% (FX tailwind fades), FY28E +15%, FY29E +14%.
segments._marginWhy: 23.8% in FY25, 25.2% in FY26, 20.4% in Q1FY27 (seasonally low). Operating leverage adds ~50 bp a year.

segments.name: SUPERFORM (active ingredients and specialty chemicals)
segments._why: ~71% of revenue is active ingredients sold to UPL Corp and UPL SAS; 29% is 'super specialty chemicals' (SSC) sold to outsiders (lubricant additives, cyanide derivatives). FY26 +1% (SSC +20%, AI −5%); Q1FY27 +14% (SSC +51%). Management targets a 55:45 AI:SSC mix in 3-4 years. FY27-29E +10% a year (SSC +25-30%, AI +3-5%).
segments._revWhy: Driver is revenue itself (including sales to group companies, removed in eliminations).
segments._marginWhy: 11.2% in FY25, 12.2% in FY26, 12.3% in Q1FY27 with higher overheads; SSC mix lifts the margin by ~50 bp a year.

segments.name: Inter-platform eliminations
segments._why: Group revenue less the sum of the four platforms: −₹6,720 cr in FY25 and −₹6,785 cr in FY26 (about 92% of SUPERFORM's active-ingredient sales, which go to UPL Corp and UPL SAS). Grows with AI sales: +5% a year.
segments._revWhy: Negative segment (engine has no elimination line).
segments._marginWhy: Zero: the EBITDA effect of eliminations sits in 'unallocated'.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Group items, exchange losses on trade balances and share of losses of associates/JVs (platform EBITDA − statutory EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: FY26: platforms ₹9,539 cr; company EBITDA ₹9,588 cr (+₹49 cr group items); statutory/Screener EBITDA ₹9,078 cr after exchange losses on trade receivables and payables (₹316 cr) and the share of losses of associates and JVs (₹194 cr), which UPL shows below EBITDA. FY25: ₹807 cr (FX ₹520 cr, associates ₹472 cr). Q1FY27: ₹222 cr (group −₹89 cr, associates ₹83 cr on Brazilian JV losses). FY27E ₹520 cr; easing to ₹380 cr by FY29E as associate losses narrow.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 capex ₹2,352 cr ($261 mn, company cash flow; Screener ₹2,406 cr) after ₹1,254 cr in FY25; Q1FY27 ₹434 cr vs ₹294 cr ('higher planned capex'). The company gave no FY27 number on its calls; CARE (30-Jun-2026) cites FY27 capex of ₹2,500-3,000 cr. We use ₹2,600 cr, then ₹2,700-2,800 cr (~4.3% of revenue). Strategic investments (e.g., ₹669 cr into the Brazilian associate Sinova in Q1FY27) are not in capex.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A ₹3,244 cr = 5.2% of average gross block (₹62,774 cr, incl. intangibles from the 2019 Arysta deal); Q1FY27 ₹832 cr (+14% YoY). 5.0% on our capex gives ₹3,390-3,660 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt company: interest income is in 'other income'.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Statutory other income ₹663 cr in FY26 (₹486 cr FY25), mostly interest income; Q1FY27 ₹217 cr. Exceptional items assumed nil.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance costs (gross, incl. factoring and exchange on borrowings)
assumptions._interestWhy: Statutory finance costs ₹3,627 cr (FY25) → ₹3,401 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 ₹852 cr (−15% YoY). Gross debt fell $850 mn in FY26 to $2.3 bn; the next $500 mn falls due Dec-2026 and $500 mn in FY28. Free cash flow of ~₹3,000 cr a year and Advanta IPO proceeds (UPL sells 7.8% in the offer for sale) reduce debt; costs also include non-recourse factoring of ₹6,800-10,200 cr of receivables. FY27E ₹3,200 cr, FY28E ₹2,850 cr, FY29E ₹2,550 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: This line is tax PLUS minority interests, as % of profit before tax (the engine has no minority line; our Net Profit is profit attributable to UPL shareholders). FY26: tax ₹937 cr (29.7%) + minorities ₹298 cr = 39.1% of PBT. Forecast: tax 28% plus minorities taking 14% (FY27E), 16.5% (FY28E) and 18.5% (FY29E) of profit after tax, rising because the fast-growing Advanta pays 21.8% to minorities (29.6% after UPL sells 7.8% in the IPO) and UPL Corp (22.2% minority) earns more as interest falls.
assumptions._payoutWhy: DPS ₹6 for FY25 and FY26 (~26% of FY26 attributable profit); ₹1 in FY24; ₹10 in FY21-23.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at one rate (cost of equity = WACC). UPL is leveraged, so we enter a WACC: cost of equity ~13.7% (beta 1.2) weighted ~75%, post-tax cost of debt ~5.5% weighted ~25% (net debt ~₹15,300 cr plus factored receivables vs ~₹45,600 cr market value) = ~11.9%, which beta 0.9 produces. The tax line includes minorities (~41% in FY29E), so FCFF is roughly UPL's share of cash flow; net debt is deducted in full, which is conservative.
dcf._tgWhy: Global crop protection grows 1-3% a year in dollars (company, AgbioInvestor); in rupees add ~2-3% depreciation: 4.5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~8% to 5%; EBITDA margin fades to 17.5%, the FY20-26 average on the statutory basis (it was 10% in the FY24 trough and 22% at the FY21 peak), because crop protection is cyclical.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~4.5% of revenue (FY26 4.5%); depreciation 5% of revenue as Arysta intangibles amortise.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Crop-protection volumes recover on share gains and new products, prices firm as the industry passes on higher costs, and Advanta keeps growing above 20%; the Advanta IPO and UPL Global listing narrow the holding-company discount.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Chinese generic oversupply returns, prices fall again as in FY24, the channel destocks in Latin America and Europe, India's monsoon disappoints and Advanta slows; working capital rises and debt does not fall.

parts.name: UPL Corp (international crop protection)
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E EBITDA (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E) × EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Post-patent crop protection: Nuvama 7x FY28E for Global Crop Protection, Anand Rathi 10x for UPL Global; Elara 6.3x and Arihant 7.5x for the whole group. Generic agchem peers (FMC, Nufarm, ADAMA) earn lower margins and trade on mid-to-high single-digit EV/EBITDA. 7x: no premium while ROCE is ~10%.

parts.name: UPL SAS (India crop protection)
parts.note: Indian crop-protection peers trade at ~12-20x trailing EV/EBITDA (Dhanuka, Rallis, Bayer CropScience); SAS has had flat revenue for two years and a volatile margin, so it sits at the bottom of that range.

parts.name: Advanta (seeds and post-harvest)
parts.note: Alpha Wave paid $350 mn for ~12.5% in Nov-2024 at an enterprise value of ~$2.8 bn (~20x Advanta's then trailing EBITDA). Anand Rathi and Nuvama use 25x. We use 15x forward: the business grows 15-20% with a 25% margin, but the IPO will price it against global seed companies on lower multiples.

parts.name: SUPERFORM (AI and specialty chemicals)
parts.note: ~70% captive active ingredients at a 12-13% margin, ~30% fast-growing specialty chemicals. Anand Rathi 15x (a 20% discount to specialty peers). 10x: between agchem manufacturers and specialty-chemical peers.

parts.name: Less: group items, FX and associates
parts.note: Exchange losses on trade balances and associate/JV losses recur every year; valued like UPL Corp.

parts.name: Less: 22.2% of UPL Corp owned by TPG, ADIA and Brookfield
parts.metricLabel: −22.21% × UPL Corp EV, plus their share of its net debt
parts.note: Minority share of UPL Corp's equity = 22.21% × (EV − net debt). Net debt of UPL Corp is not disclosed; we allocate ~₹13,000 cr (about 85% of group net debt, in line with Nuvama's split and UPL Global's guided 2.0-2.3x net debt/EBITDA), so 22.21% × ₹13,000 cr = ₹2,890 cr is added back.

parts.name: Less: 9.1% of UPL SAS owned by TPG, ADIA and Brookfield
parts.note: UPL SAS is assumed debt-free.

parts.name: Less: 21.8% of Advanta owned by KKR and Alpha Wave
parts.note: UPL group owns 78.21% (Feb-2026). The IPO is an offer for sale, so it moves value from shares to cash and does not change the total; Advanta is assumed debt-free.

parts.name: Less: net debt at Sep-27E
parts.metricLabel: Model net debt at the target date (½ Mar-27E + ½ Mar-28E)
parts.note: Borrowings incl. leases less cash and all investments (investments include ~₹2,000 cr of stakes in associates and JVs, taken at book value). Excludes ₹10,231 cr of receivables factored without recourse (Mar-26).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How most of the street values UPL (Motilal Oswal 12x, Jefferies 14x Jun-28E, Anand Rathi 15x and Antique 16x FY28E). Derivation: UPL’s one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on the house rule (forwardMedian: trough years left out) is 16.6x; forward FY25 and FY26 are excluded as trough years (EPS ₹11.5 and ₹22.8, below half of FY23’s ₹45.6) and the FY24 loss drops out automatically (all dates: 22.5x). Indian crop-protection peers trade ~25% below their five-year median P/E (median ratio 0.75; Coromandel, a fertiliser company, left out). 16.6x × 0.75 ≈ 12.4x → 12x (nearest whole multiple); no premium while ROE (8-11%) is below the ~13.7% cost of equity and minorities take a rising share of profit: 12x. Bull 14x (Jefferies’ long-term average), bear 9x.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: Each platform on Sep-28E EV/EBITDA, less group items, UPL's minority partners' share of each platform and net debt; no holding-company discount. Shows what the platforms could be worth if listed separately.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: 15-year FCFF at ~11.9% WACC, terminal growth 5%, less group net debt.
